tagline: Fuel pipeline billing is failing. Stop the breach before critical operations halt.

incidents.title: Credential Stuffing Spike
incidents.hook: 100,000 failed logins per minute from distributed bot IPs.
incidents.alert: AUTH GATEWAY CPU 98% — High-volume credential stuffing detected
incidents.stakes_line: Customer account lockouts threaten morning gas pump terminals.

evidence.label: LATENCY / FAIL RATE
evidence.content: Auth API p99 latency spiked from 45ms to 1840ms. Error rate 84%.

evidence.label: SOC SLACK CHANNEL
evidence.content: Ops Lead: Retail terminals report login timeouts. What is our first mitigation?

incidents.question: What is your immediate tactical move?

options.text: Apply immediate IP reputation blocklist and adaptive rate-limiting at edge.
options.outcome: Bot volume drops 92% instantly; valid traffic resumes flowing to auth cluster.
options.why: Edge rate limiting sheds distributed volume without burdening origin services.

options.text: Shut down the customer authentication service entirely until root cause is identified.
options.outcome: Total outage across all 4,200 stations; executive panic ensues.
options.why: Self-inflicted denial of service creates the exact disaster the attacker wanted.

options.text: Force an immediate password reset email to all 2.4 million customers.
options.outcome: Mail servers crash under queue overload; customer support phone lines collapse.
options.why: Mass password resets create secondary outages before containment is in place.

options.text: Spin up additional backend authentication servers to absorb the bot traffic.
options.outcome: Database connections saturate within minutes; cloud bill spikes $18,000.
options.why: Scaling against an unbounded botnet only shifts the bottleneck to the database.

debrief.concept: Isolate volume at edge before investigating
debrief.rule_of_thumb: Filter malicious volume at the perimeter; never make your origin absorb DDoS.
debrief.why_best_works: Edge defenses absorb packet volume with zero overhead on backend databases.
debrief.real_world_note: Akamai and Cloudflare edge scrubbing mitigate 99% of bulk credential attacks.
debrief.next_teaser: The perimeter held, but internal telemetry reveals an insider host behaving strangely.

incidents.title: Ransomware Lateral Pivot
incidents.hook: SMB probes spreading through accounting laptops towards domain controllers.
incidents.alert: EDR CRITICAL — Mimikatz memory dump detected on finance workstation
incidents.stakes_line: Active Directory compromise means total network lockout within the hour.

evidence.label: EDR TELEMETRY
evidence.content: lsass.exe memory read by unknown binary C:\Users\acct1\AppData\Temp\svchost.exe

evidence.label: NETWORK TOPOLOGY
evidence.content: Host 10.14.2.88 executing outbound TCP 445 sweeps against 10.14.0.0/16 subnet.

evidence.label: CISO DIRECT MESSAGE
evidence.content: CISO: Do not let them touch the primary domain controller. What is your call?

incidents.question: What is the primary containment action?

options.text: Isolate the infected host network interface via EDR and sever VLAN cross-talk.
options.outcome: Host is quarantined instantly; lateral sweeps hit firewall drop counters.
options.why: Network-level host isolation arrests spread while preserving memory for forensics.

options.text: Reboot the infected machine into safe mode to terminate malware processes.
options.outcome: Volatile RAM evidence wiped; persistence runkey re-infects host on boot.
options.why: Rebooting destroys invaluable memory evidence and triggers persistence mechanisms.

options.text: Email the finance department asking employees to disconnect Wi-Fi cables.
options.outcome: Too slow; attacker compromises 14 more machines before anyone reads email.
options.why: Human-dependent mitigation during an active automated worm fails every time.

options.text: Change the domain admin password in Active Directory console.
options.outcome: Password updated, but existing Kerberos golden tickets remain valid and usable.
options.why: Password change does not invalidate active sessions or cached Kerberos tickets.

debrief.rule_of_thumb: Cut the cord at the hypervisor or EDR; never reboot an actively exploited host.
debrief.why_best_works: Preserves volatile artifacts while cutting off command-and-control channels.
debrief.real_world_note: Colonial Pipeline halted fuel delivery largely due to lack of OT/IT isolation.
debrief.next_teaser: Workstations are safe, but cloud audit logs show an AWS access key exfiltrating data.

incidents.title: Cloud S3 Exfiltration
incidents.concept: IAM key invalidation & bucket policy lock
incidents.hook: An engineer's leaked API key is dumping customer transaction records.
incidents.alert: GUARDDUTY — Unusual S3 GetObject volume from unknown IP in Eastern Europe
incidents.stakes_line: 500 GB of plaintext billing records will trigger massive regulatory penalties.

evidence.label: CLOUDTRAIL EVENT
evidence.content: eventName: GetObject, bucket: corp-billing-archive, userAgent: aws-cli/2.11

evidence.label: EGRESS BANDWIDTH
evidence.content: Outbound S3 egress at 1.4 Gbps. 180 GB transferred in last 12 minutes.

evidence.label: LEGAL TEAM
evidence.content: Legal: If personal identifiable records leak publicly, mandatory breach disclosure begins.

incidents.question: How do you halt the data exfiltration immediately?

options.text: Deactivate IAM access key, apply explicit Deny S3 bucket policy, revoke sessions.
options.outcome: API requests immediately return 403 Forbidden; egress flatlines to zero.
options.why: Combining IAM key deactivation with an explicit bucket deny halts all active access.

options.text: Delete the S3 bucket to ensure no further records can be accessed.
options.outcome: 10 years of business financial records permanently erased; production down.
options.why: Destructive containment destroys your company's own primary business data.

options.text: Message the engineer on Slack asking if they shared their credentials.
options.outcome: Exfiltration finishes downloading all 500 GB while waiting for a reply.
options.why: Never investigate before cutting the active unauthorized access conduit.

options.text: Download the bucket contents to your local laptop to see what is missing.
options.outcome: Saturates company VPN bandwidth and violates corporate compliance policies.
options.why: Duplicating sensitive data to unapproved endpoints compounds the legal exposure.

debrief.concept: Kill credentials and enforce explicit deny
debrief.rule_of_thumb: Deactivate identity credentials first, then attach explicit Deny resource policies.
debrief.why_best_works: Explicit Deny overrides all existing allow policies across federated roles.
debrief.real_world_note: Capital One S3 breach stemmed from misconfigured WAF IAM role permissions.
debrief.next_teaser: Cloud access is locked, but the CI/CD pipeline just built a suspicious binary.

incidents.title: Supply Chain Dependency Poisoning
incidents.hook: A compromised npm package is executing shell scripts during production build.
incidents.alert: PIPELINE FAILED — Postinstall hook attempted connection to external pastebin
incidents.stakes_line: Deploying this scheduled release injects backdoors into 80,000 retail apps.

evidence.label: GITHUB ACTIONS LOG
evidence.content: npm install: package 'event-telemetry-core@2.1.4' running preinstall curl script

evidence.label: DIFF VIEWER
evidence.content: package-lock.json modified 40 minutes ago by automated dependency bot.

evidence.label: RELEASE MANAGER
evidence.content: Release Manager: Production deploy freeze is scheduled in 10 minutes. Can we ship?

incidents.question: What is the decisive response for this compromised release?

options.text: Halt deployment, pin previous known-good hash in lockfile, quarantine artifact registry.
options.outcome: Release halted cleanly; poison package isolated before touching production.
options.why: Stopping the pipeline and pinning cryptographically verified hashes stops supply chain attack.

options.text: Run the deploy with '--ignore-scripts' flag to bypass the build warning.
options.outcome: Poisoned library still packages into bundle; backdoor goes live to customers.
options.why: Ignoring pipeline security alerts is how backdoors bypass production safeguards.

options.text: Submit a bug report to the open-source npm maintainer and wait for a fix.
options.outcome: Release deadline passes with unresolved vulnerability looming over cluster.
options.why: Open source maintainer response times cannot dictate real-time incident containment.

options.text: Delete node_modules and re-run the build to see if the error was transient.
options.outcome: Rebuild pulls the identical malicious package again, wasting critical time.
options.why: Dependency poisoning is deterministic; rebuilding without pinning reproduces the exploit.

debrief.concept: Cryptographic lockfiles and immutable build gates
debrief.rule_of_thumb: Never bypass failing build security gates; pin immutable SHA hashes.
debrief.why_best_works: Lockfiles ensure reproducible builds and prevent silent malicious version upgrades.
debrief.real_world_note: SolarWinds and event-stream incidents succeeded via untracked build dependencies.
debrief.next_teaser: Final challenge: the adversary is attempting a direct memory compromise of the root key.

incidents.title: Root Key Exfiltration Zero-Day
incidents.concept: Root key revocation & emergency failover protocol
incidents.hook: Master cryptographic signing certificates are being tampered with.
incidents.alert: HSM ALARM — Multiple unauthorized tamper-pin attempts on master keystore
incidents.stakes_line: Loss of the master key allows attacker to permanently forge company credentials.

evidence.label: HSM AUDIT TRAIL
evidence.content: KEY_MGMT: ExportPrivateKey attempted on slot 0 (Root CA). Policy violation 0xFA.

evidence.label: SYSTEM HEALTH
evidence.content: HSM anti-tamper sensors triggered. Zeroize countdown timer: STANDBY.

evidence.label: CHIEF INFORMATION OFFICER
evidence.content: CIO: If they steal that root private key, our entire corporate trust chain is dead.

incidents.question: What is the ultimate fail-safe action to save the enterprise?

options.text: Trigger emergency cold zeroize of compromised slot and activate offline air-gapped backup.
options.outcome: Private key securely destroyed; backup HSM initialized from vault safely.
options.why: Zeroizing destroys the prize before exfiltration; offline backups preserve business continuity.

options.text: Unplug the HSM power cable from the rack without running shutdown scripts.
options.outcome: Internal battery backup keeps memory live; key extraction completes on reserve power.
options.why: Enterprise HSMs have onboard battery backups specifically designed for sudden power cuts.

options.text: Try SSHing into the HSM operating system to check the active process list.
options.outcome: SSH fails because HSMs do not expose shell access; 8 precious minutes lost.
options.why: Hardware appliances do not run standard shell daemons; protocol commands are required.

options.text: Change the password on the admin dashboard.
options.outcome: Attacker is using physical bus taps; software password changes have zero effect.
options.why: Physical tamper attacks require physical zeroization, not application credentials.

debrief.concept: Zeroize compromise and switch to air-gapped root
debrief.rule_of_thumb: When master keys are threatened, zeroize immediately. Keys can rotate; stolen trust is forever.
debrief.why_best_works: Denies the attacker their ultimate objective while maintaining recovery paths via cold storage.
debrief.real_world_note: Certificate Authorities maintain air-gapped ceremony keys in physical bank vaults.
debrief.next_teaser: Case solved! The timeline has stabilized and the enterprise is secure.
